payload.prompt:
Paint historical key art in hand-painted 2D animation style with soft oil-brush character. Use one dominant subject with a modest set of supporting groups: enough context for a lived-in scene, but no exhaustive inventory. Use only the element families selected below.

Allowed scene elements ONLY: One monumental limestone structure visibly under active construction; one compact stack of limestone blocks; one small group of builders; one timber lifting frame; one small work shelter; one material handcart; one compact timber stack; one attached scaffold group; one low temporary site boundary.

Composition: A general illustration of building a great wonder, usable across the construction process rather than depicting a named chronological stage. Use a moderately low three-quarter view: the imposing stone structure spans the central middle distance, with its principal opening at right-center. Substantial lower arches and rising upper walls establish the monument's ambition; an unfinished upper silhouette makes ongoing construction clear. Keep its architectural purpose broadly civic and monumental, without specific sacred emblems, a distinctive historical landmark or the exact layout of the five-stage hall. The attached scaffold follows one side of the structure, and the smaller lifting frame raises a block beside it; these simple actions express human labor and engineering. Group builders at the structure's foot and on the scaffold as one coherent working activity, with no separate designer or official group. Place stone, handcart and timber together in a compact delivery zone beside the approach; the low shelter and boundary enclose that same zone. The monument is the first read, followed by lifting and labor, then supporting materials. Keep the whole construction silhouette visible and the foreground shallow. Do not depict an empty surveyed plot, a foundation-only excavation, a fully finished ceremonial building or a montage of several stages. Retain the selected scene complexity; no extra landscape, animal, vehicle or material categories.

Use large joined color shapes, broad light-and-shadow planes and a few deliberate brush strokes. The subject takes most of the visual weight; supporting forms are smaller, softer and lower in contrast. Keep recognizable proportions, but simplify repeated structure and omit surface microdetail. No individually drawn leaves, grass blades, bricks, cracks, wood grain, faces or costume ornament. Use warm ochre and terracotta against cool slate-blue shadows, with restrained accents.

Paint one continuous full-bleed scene across the entire requested canvas, edge to edge and corner to corner. Continue the painted setting naturally to every edge, including the top and bottom. No white or black bars, unpainted margins, letterboxing, borders, matting or inset picture. Keep the complete principal subject comfortably inside the canvas without creating an inner frame. Surrounding space remains painted atmosphere and ground with the same visual style; do not fill it with additional object categories or a vast empty foreground.

Keep to the listed element families. Each support stays a compact group; do not expand it into many new object types, occupations, material varieties, animal species or scenery. Small same-type repetition is allowed within a group. Keep secondary forms quiet and the main subject unmistakable. No busy panorama, photographic detail, 3D rendering, collage, readable text, logo, watermark or UI.
